# API reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_api_docs.ts from src/api.ts. Do not edit; run `node scripts/gen_api_docs.ts`. -->

mpljs mirrors matplotlib's object-oriented API. Positional arguments come first; keyword arguments
go in a trailing plain object (`ax.plot(x, y, { color: "C1", lw: 2 })`). Aliases are listed as
`name | alias`. A keyword mpljs does not support is an error, never silently ignored.

## Functions

### `subplots(kwargs?)`

subplots({ style, rc, figsize, dpi }) -> [fig, ax]

## Figure

Create one with `subplots()` or `new Figure({ style, rc, figsize, dpi })`.

### `Figure.add_subplot()`

add_subplot() — the figure's Axes, placed by figure.subplot.* (one per figure in mpljs).

### `Figure.text(x, y, s, kwargs?)`

Figure-level text in figure coordinates (0..1).

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `color | c`, `fontsize | size`, `ha | horizontalalignment`, `va | verticalalignment`

### `Figure.suptitle(s, kwargs?)`

suptitle(s, { color|c, fontsize|size, fontweight|weight }) — centred figure title (figure.titlesize/titleweight).

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `color | c`, `fontsize | size`, `fontweight | weight`

### `Figure.supxlabel(s, kwargs?)`

supxlabel(s, { color|c, fontsize|size, fontweight|weight }) — figure-level x label at the bottom.

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `color | c`, `fontsize | size`, `fontweight | weight`

### `Figure.supylabel(s, kwargs?)`

supylabel(s, { color|c, fontsize|size, fontweight|weight }) — figure-level y label at the left, rotated.

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `color | c`, `fontsize | size`, `fontweight | weight`

### `Figure.subplots_adjust(kwargs?)`

subplots_adjust({ left, bottom, right, top }) — the Axes box in figure fractions (wspace/hspace accepted, no effect with one Axes).

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `left`, `right`, `bottom`, `top`, `wspace`, `hspace`

### `Figure.tight_layout(kwargs?)`

tight_layout({ pad = 1.08, h_pad, w_pad, rect }) — _tight_layout.get_tight_layout_figure for the one subplot cell mpljs has (an Axes and its twins): lay out now, measure Axes.get_tightbbox, then subplots_adjust so the decorations fit inside the figure with `pad` font sizes to spare. As in matplotlib it runs once, at call time: call it after the plot is complete.

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `pad`, `h_pad`, `w_pad`, `rect`

### `Figure.toScene()`

Run layout; one trace per run.

### `Figure.toSVG()`

The figure as an SVG document string, as matplotlib's SVG backend writes it.

### `Figure.svgChunks()`

The SVG as a generator of string chunks.

### `Figure.svgStream()`

The SVG as a byte stream (Workers, browsers, Node).

### `Figure.toRGBA()`

RGBA8 pixels (straight alpha), rasterized like matplotlib's Agg backend.

### `Figure.toPNG()`

PNG bytes via the platform's CompressionStream (Workers, browsers, Node ≥ 18).

### `Figure.toPNGSync()`

PNG bytes, synchronously, with the built-in deflate.

### `Figure.pngStream()`

PNG as a byte stream: IHDR first, IDAT chunks as the compressor yields them.

## Axes

Returned by `subplots()`, `fig.add_subplot()` and `ax.twinx()`.

### `Axes.twinx()`

A second Axes sharing this one's x axis, with its y axis on the right.

### `Axes.set_xscale(s)`

set_xscale('linear' | 'log')

### `Axes.set_yscale(s)`

set_yscale('linear' | 'log')

### `Axes.plot(...args)`

plot(y) | plot(x, y) | plot(x, y, fmt), with an optional trailing kwargs object.

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `color | c`, `alpha`, `linestyle | ls`, `marker`, `linewidth | lw`, `markersize | ms`, `markeredgewidth | mew`, `markerfacecolor | mfc`, `markeredgecolor | mec`, `label`, `clip_on | clipon | clip`

### `Axes.bar(x, height, kwargs?)`

bar(x, height, { width, bottom, align, color|facecolor|fc, edgecolor|ec, linewidth|lw, alpha, label, clip_on }) — vertical bars.

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `o===vertical?width:height`, `o===vertical?bottom:left`, `align`, `color | facecolor | fc`, `edgecolor | ec`, `linewidth | lw`, `alpha`, `label`, `clip_on | clipon | clip`

### `Axes.barh(y, width, kwargs?)`

barh(y, width, { height, left, align, color|facecolor|fc, edgecolor|ec, linewidth|lw, alpha, label, clip_on }) — horizontal bars; `left` offsets each bar (Gantt and waterfall charts).

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `o===vertical?width:height`, `o===vertical?bottom:left`, `align`, `color | facecolor | fc`, `edgecolor | ec`, `linewidth | lw`, `alpha`, `label`, `clip_on | clipon | clip`

### `Axes.fill_between(xRaw, y1Raw, ...rest)`

fill_between(x, y1, y2 = 0, { color, alpha, label }) — a FillBetweenPolyCollection with no edges.

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `color`, `facecolor | fc`, `alpha`, `linewidth | lw`, `label`, `clip_on | clipon | clip`

### `Axes.get transData()`

The transform tokens text() understands, named as in matplotlib.

### `Axes.get transAxes()`

Axes-fraction coordinates for text(): (0, 0) bottom left, (1, 1) top right.

### `Axes.text(xRaw, yRaw, s, kwargs?)`

text(x, y, s, { transform, color, fontsize, ha, va }) — data coordinates unless transform: ax.transAxes.

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `transform`, `color | c`, `fontsize | size`, `ha | horizontalalignment`, `va | verticalalignment`, `fontweight | weight`, `clip_on | clipon | clip`

### `Axes.annotate(text, xy, kwargs?)`

annotate(text, xy, { xytext, xycoords, textcoords, arrowprops })

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `xytext`, `xycoords`, `textcoords`, `arrowprops`, `clip_on | clipon | clip`

### `Axes.scatter(xRaw, yRaw, kwargs?)`

scatter(x, y, { s, c, marker, alpha, edgecolors, linewidths, zorder, clip_on })

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `s`, `marker`, `alpha`, `c | color`, `edgecolors | edgecolor`, `linewidths | linewidth`, `label`, `clip_on | clipon | clip`

### `Axes.axvspan(xmin, xmax, kwargs?)`

axvspan: vertical span in data x and axes-fraction y

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `ymin`, `ymax`, `color`, `facecolor | fc`, `edgecolor | ec`, `linewidth | lw`, `alpha`, `label`, `clip_on | clipon | clip`

### `Axes.axhspan(ymin, ymax, kwargs?)`

axhspan: horizontal span in data y and axes-fraction x

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `xmin`, `xmax`, `color`, `facecolor | fc`, `edgecolor | ec`, `linewidth | lw`, `alpha`, `label`, `clip_on | clipon | clip`

### `Axes.set_title(s, kwargs?)`

set_title(s, { loc: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' })

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `loc`, `fontweight | weight`

### `Axes.get spines()`

ax.spines['left'].set_visible(False) etc.

### `Axes.tick_params(kwargs?)`

Tick parameters: axis {'x','y','both'}, which {'major','minor','both'}, length, width, colors, labelsize, bottom/top/left/right, labelbottom/labelleft, pad, direction.

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `axis`, `which`, `length`, `width`, `colors | color`, `labelsize`, `bottom`, `top`, `left`, `right`, `labelbottom`, `labelleft`, `pad`, `direction`

### `Axes.set_xlabel(s)`

set_xlabel(s) — x axis label; '\n' starts a new line.

### `Axes.set_ylabel(s)`

set_ylabel(s) — y axis label, rotated 90°; '\n' starts a new line.

### `Axes.set_xlim(...args)`

set_xlim(lo, hi) or set_xlim([lo, hi]); lo > hi inverts the axis.

### `Axes.set_ylim(...args)`

set_ylim(lo, hi) or set_ylim([lo, hi]); lo > hi inverts the axis (top-down Gantt rows).

### `Axes.set_xticks(t)`

set_xticks(locs) — fixed major tick locations.

### `Axes.set_yticks(t)`

set_yticks(locs) — fixed major tick locations.

### `Axes.set_xticklabels(l, kwargs?)`

set_xticklabels(labels, { color|c, fontsize|size, fontweight|weight }): the kwargs style every label set here.

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `color | c`, `fontsize | size`, `fontweight | weight`

### `Axes.set_yticklabels(l, kwargs?)`

set_yticklabels(labels, { color|c, fontsize|size, fontweight|weight }): the kwargs style every label set here.

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `color | c`, `fontsize | size`, `fontweight | weight`

### `Axes.get_xticklabels()`

The major tick labels as Text handles: get_text(), set_fontweight(), set_color(), set_fontsize().

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `color | c`, `fontsize | size`, `fontweight | weight`

### `Axes.get_yticklabels()`

The major y tick labels as Text handles (see get_xticklabels).

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `color | c`, `fontsize | size`, `fontweight | weight`

### `Axes.grid(visible?, kwargs?)`

grid(visible?, { which, axis, color|c, linewidth|lw, linestyle|ls, alpha }) — Axes.grid. As in matplotlib: line kwargs imply visible=True, visible=null toggles, and the line properties stick to the chosen axes and tick families (major, minor) for later grid() calls. A kwargs object alone, grid({ ... }), is grid(null, { ... }).

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `axis`, `which`, `color | c`, `linewidth | lw`, `linestyle | ls`, `alpha`

### `Axes.legend(kwargs?)`

legend({ loc, ncols|ncol, frameon, fontsize }) — entries come from artists with a label.

Keyword arguments (unknown keys throw): `loc`, `ncols | ncol`, `frameon`, `fontsize`

### `Axes.spec()`

The Axes as plain data (what layout consumes); mostly for tooling and tests.
